# Tabverse

> Tabverse is a Chrome extension that turns a window full of related tabs into a
> named workspace - a "tabverse" - that can be put down and picked up again,
> with its own notes, todos, bookmarks, closed-tab history and AI chat.

Tabverse is a Manifest V3 extension for Chrome 140 or newer, local first: every
tabverse and everything attached to it lives in IndexedDB in the browser
profile, with no account, no network and no telemetry. Pairing with a sync
server is optional and is the only thing that ever sends data anywhere; the
server is `tabversed`, an open source Go program the user runs (the project also
runs one for people who do not want to).

The links below are the user manual on this site, in reading order. Each page is
the authority for its subject; this file is the index an agent should start from.

## Getting started

- [Get Started](docs/intro/): what a tabverse is, both ways to install (Chrome
  Web Store, or a release zip loaded unpacked), the popup's actions, the first
  tabverse, and where the optional server sync fits.
- [Install from source](docs/install-from-source/): for developers - clone,
  `pnpm install`, `pnpm run dev` or `pnpm run build`, load `dist/` unpacked,
  and why an unpacked build has its own extension id and empty profile.
- [Tabverses](docs/basic-usage/tabverses/): the core page. Creating a tabverse
  (one per window, at most), the manager interface, save & close, restoring,
  searching saved tabverses, and exporting/importing `.tabverse` files.

## The tools attached to a tabverse

- [Todo](docs/basic-usage/todo/): the checklist for this tabverse.
- [Note](docs/basic-usage/note/): Markdown notes, with the editor's commands.
- [Bookmark](docs/basic-usage/bookmark/): bookmarks scoped to the tabverse
  rather than to Chrome's bookmark store.
- [History](docs/basic-usage/history/): the tabs closed from this tabverse - up
  to 999, one row per url, not a copy of Chrome's history - with search,
  grouping by site, reopen/undo, save-as-bookmark and forget.
- [On-device AI](docs/advanced-usage/ai/): AI Chat, summarizing a page into a
  note and naming a tabverse, where Chrome ships its built-in model; plus "view
  page content as Markdown", which needs no model.

One tool can be pinned to the top of the tools column, the pinned tool and the
selected tool are remembered across reloads, and a tool's own header stays put
while its rows scroll. The details are in [Tabverses](docs/basic-usage/tabverses/).

## Search and sync

- [Omni search](docs/advanced-usage/omni-search/): one search over tab titles and
  urls, history, notes, todos and bookmarks - a local scan without a server, the
  server's full-text index with one, falling back to the local scan when the
  server cannot be reached. Results are catalogued by tabverse, not as loose
  records.
- [Sync with a server](docs/advanced-usage/server-sync/): what syncs, the two
  pairing paths (the project's server with an email sign-in, or any
  `tabversed` with a single-use pairing code), device tokens, and the privacy
  posture. A device is paired, not logged in.
- [Self-host a server](docs/self-host-server/): running `tabversed` - a single Go
  binary over SQLite, configuration, and TLS.
- [Server console](docs/server-console/): the account surface - paired devices,
  revoking a token, the read-only view of stored data, and sign-in.

## Facts an agent should not guess

- A window holds **at most one** tabverse. Creating one in a window that already
  has one asks first, and the open tabs become part of the new tabverse.
- **Nothing is closed without the user asking.** "Load to Current" is a merge:
  open tabs are kept, a saved tab whose url is already open is reused, and only
  missing tabs are opened. "Load to New" opens a new window. "Switch to
  Tabverse" focuses the window that already holds it.
- **Delete has no confirmation and no undo** - it removes the tabverse and
  everything attached to it.
- Edits are saved as they happen; there is no save button. "Save & close" only
  flushes a pending change and closes the manager tab, leaving the window open.
- A `.tabverse` file is one JSON document holding the tabverse, its tabs and tab
  groups, notes, todos, bookmarks and history. Import always creates a **new,
  independent** tabverse (ids are reminted, the name becomes `Imported: <name> -
  <time>`), and it lands in the saved list without being opened.
- Data lives in IndexedDB in the browser (tab previews are a cache keyed by tab
  id, swept when a tab closes). Nothing leaves the device until a device is
  paired with a server, and then only the content - tab urls and titles, notes,
  todos, bookmarks, history.
- Without Chrome's built-in model the AI actions are disabled and the chat says
  so; the page-to-Markdown action still works.
- An unpacked (source or release-zip) install has a different extension id from
  the store build, hence a separate, empty profile; a `.tabverse` export is the
  way to move data between them.

## Support

- [r/tabverse](https://www.reddit.com/r/tabverse/): the community, where support
  and discussion happen.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/liyu1981/tabverse): source, releases,
  issues and discussions.
- [Chrome Web Store listing](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tabverse/lffblcippngalmglinedcbmikkncihdm):
  the released build.
